# 2026 MCM Problem C: Data With The Stars

Source: COMAP official 2026 MCM/ICM problem statement (https://contest.comap.com/undergraduate/contests/mcm/contests/2026/problems/2026_MCM_Problem_C.pdf).

Data file attached: 2026_MCM_Problem_C_Data.csv (seasons 1-34, contestant info, results, weekly judge scores).

---

Problem C: Data With The Stars



Dancing with the Stars (DWTS) is the American version of an international television franchise
based on the British show “Strictly Come Dancing” (“Come Dancing” originally). Versions of
the show have appeared in Albania, Argentina, Australia, China, France, India, and many other
countries. The U.S. version, the focus of this problem, has completed 34 seasons.

Celebrities are partnered with professional dancers and then perform dances each week. A panel
of expert judges scores each couple’s dance, and fans vote (by phone or online) for their favorite
couple that week. Fans can vote once or multiple times up to a limit announced each week.
Further, fans vote for the star they wish to keep, but cannot vote to eliminate a star. The judge
and fan votes are combined in order to determine which couple to eliminate (the lowest
combined score) that week. Three (in some seasons more) couples reach the finals and in the
week of the finals the combined scores from fans and judges are used to rank them from 1st to 3rd
(or 4th, 5th).

There are many possible methods of combining fan votes and judge scores. In the first two
seasons of the U.S. show, the combination was based on ranks. Season 2 concerns (due to
celebrity contestant Jerry Rice who was a finalist despite very low judge scores) led to a
modification to use percentages instead of ranks. Examples of these two approaches are provided
in the Appendix.

In season 27, another “controversy” occurred when celebrity contestant Bobby Bones won
despite consistently low judges scores. In response, starting in season 28 a slight modification to
the elimination process was made. The bottom two contestants were identified using the
combined judge scores and fan votes, and then during the live show the judges voted to select
which of these two to eliminate. Around this same season, the producers also returned to using
the method of ranks to combine judges scores with fan votes as in seasons one and two. The
exact season this change occurred is not known, but it is reasonable to assume it was season 28.

Judge scores are meant to reflect which dancers are technically better, although there is some
subjectivity in what makes a dance better. Fan votes are likely much more subjective, influenced
by the quality of the dance, but also the popularity and charisma of the celebrity. Show producers
might actually prefer, to some extent, conflicts in opinions and votes as such occurrences boost
fan interest and excitement.

Data with judges scores and contestant information is provided and described below. You may
choose to include additional information or other data at your discretion, but you must
completely document the sources. Use the data to:
• Develop a mathematical model (or models) to produce estimated fan votes (which are
unknown and a closely guarded secret) for each contestant for the weeks they competed.
o Does your model correctly estimate fan votes that lead to results consistent with who
was eliminated each week? Provide measures of the consistency.
o How much certainty is there in the fan vote totals you produced, and is that certainty
always the same for each contestant/week? Provide measures of your certainty for the
estimates.

• Use your fan vote estimates with the rest of the data to:
o Compare and contrast the results produced by the two approaches used by the show to
combine judge and fan votes (i.e. rank and percentage) across seasons (i.e. apply both
approaches to each season). If differences in outcomes exist, does one method seem
to favor fan votes more than the other?
o Examine the two voting methods applied to specific celebrities where there was
“controversy”, meaning differences between judges and fans. Would the choice of
method to combine judge scores and fan votes have led to the same result for each of
these contestants? How would including the additional approach of having judges
choose which of the bottom two couples to eliminate each week impact the results?
Some examples you might consider (there may also be others you identified):
 season 2 –Jerry Rice, runner up despite the lowest judges scores in 5 weeks.
 season 4 – Billy Ray Cyrus was 5th despite last place judge scores in 6 weeks.
 season 11 – Bristol Palin was 3rd with the lowest judge scores 12 times.
 season 27 – Bobby Bones won the despite consistently low judges scores
o Based on your analysis, which of the two methods would you recommend using for
future seasons and why? Would you suggest including the additional approach of
judges choosing from the bottom two couples?

• Use the data including your fan vote estimates to develop a model that analyzes the impact of
various pro dancers as well as characteristics for the celebrities available in the data (age,
industry, etc). How much do such things impact how well a celebrity will do in the
competition? Do they impact judges scores and fan votes in the same way?

• Propose another system using fan votes and judge scores each week that you believe is more
“fair” (or “better” in some other way such as making the show more exciting for the fans).
Provide support for why your approach should be adopted by the show producers.

• Produce a report of no more than 25 pages with your findings and include a one- to two-page
memo summarizing your results with advice for producers of DWTS on the impact of how
judge and fan votes are combined with recommendations for how to do so in future seasons.

MODEL PLAN (from Master Plan):
## Model 2: Judge–Fan Behavioral Attribution (identification of pro/partner effect, industry, age on judge scores vs fan shares; platform-shift decomposition; hierarchical Bayesian response surfaces)

### Purpose
Answer the third bullet with clean causal logic: how much do the pro dancer's skill/track record,
the celebrity's industry, age, and prior fame drive *judge scores* and *fan votes*?
Key subtlety the judges' reading of the problem statement demands: judge scores and fan votes are
incentivized differently (technical merit vs popularity), so effects must be estimated SEPARATELY
on the two outcome surfaces, never co-mingled. Model 2 consumes Model 1's posterior fan shares
(ρ = E[φ]) alongside the observed judge totals.

### Mathematical Formulation

Two parallel hierarchical Bayesian response models (shared structure, different outcomes y):
  **Judge surface:**  y^J_{c,w} = z(x_{c,w}) normalized (within-week, dance-count aware)
  **Fan surface:**    y^F_{c,w} = logit(φ̂_{c,w} + δ) with a tiny offset (weekly share ∈ (0,1))

Model (linear mixed with heterogeneous slopes, fit separately for y^J and y^F):
  y_{c,w} = α_s + π_{p(c, s)} + ι_{ind(c)} + f(age_{c}) + g(weekcounter_{c,w})
            + θ·(pro × industry interaction) + u_c + ε_{c,w}

where
  - α_s: season fixed effect (production drift, judge panel size, era),
  - π_p: **pro-dancer random effect** — the quantity of interest (54 pros, min 2 seasons each).
    Prior: π_p ~ N(π̄, τ_π²), hyperprior τ_π ~ HalfNormal(0.5). Pooling handles sparse pros.
  - ι_ind: industry effect (25 levels, hierarchical: ι ~ N(I·bar-industry, τ_I²)),
  - f(age): a restricted cubic spline (4 knots at 20/30/45/65) so age effects are flexible
    but monotone-plausible; identical functional form for both surfaces,
  - g(weekcounter): within-run learning curve (celebrities improve) — fitted separately for
    judge surface (should be positive) and fan surface (may be negative — fans punish formality),
  - u_c: contestant random intercept N(0, σ_u²) (charisma/fame residual, not explained by covariates),
  - ε_{c,w} ~ N(0, σ²) (per-week noise).

**Key decomposition (the headline result):** for each covariate class k,
  R_k = Var_k[ŷ] / Var[ŷ]  (fraction of outcome variance explained by class k),
reported for k ∈ {pro, industry, age, week, season, residual-fame u_c}, side-by-side for the
judge and fan surfaces. The equality or divergence of R^J_k vs R^F_k is the "do they impact both
in the same way?" answer, with a permutation test for each (shuffle the covariate within season;
1,000 shuffles → null band of R_k).

**Anti-instrumental check (mandatory, honest selection):** pro-dancer assignments are NOT random
(Bean Counting error: pros are assigned by producers possibly related to celebrity caliber). We
therefore (i) report the naive R_k (no correction), and (ii) a "restricted" R_k from a mediation
specification where celebrity fixed effects absorb ability: π̂_p restricted = π̂_p − μ_pα(s Selection)
from a busy-direction decomposition. Final statements carry both numbers with a plain-language
caveat ("pro effect on judge scores is partially a sorting artifact; the honest lower bound is…").

### Solution Strategy (10–20 lines)
Python: statsmodels (mixed lm with var_identification via `mixedlm`), PyMC for the spline +
hierarchical version (NUTS, 4×800 draws — feasible: ~421 runs × ≈7 weeks avg = 2,777 rows),
scipy for splines (`scipy.interpolate` design matrices), permutation tests vectorized in numpy.
1. Merge `week_scores.csv` (per-week judge y^J) with `model1_fanshare.csv` (y^F) on
   (season, celebrity_name, week); merge `contestants.csv` covariates and `partner_primary`.
2. Filter: exclude weeks after a withdrawal (incomplete market) and flag multi-dance weeks
   with a fixed effect (utils the `multi_dance_week` shared flag).
3. Fit judge surface → coefficient table π̂_p, ι̂_ind, f̂(age), ĝ; repeat for fan surface.
4. Compute the variance-decomposition table R_k and the permutation p-values.
5. Rank pros by posterior E[π_p] with 95% CrI (top-5 and bottom-5 list; Derek Hough-type
   validation: known-elite pros should emerge).
6. Produce the "same-direction?" matrix: covariate k × surface (judge/fan) with effect sign,
   size, and a 2-sided bootstrap CI computed on 2,000 cluster bootstraps by season.
7. Deliver a small "counterfactual swap" exhibit: predicted placement distribution if an average
   celebrity (median everything) is paired with the best vs the median pro.

### Expected Outputs
- `model2_effects.csv`: long table covariate × level × surface × estimate × CrI × permutation p.
- `model2_decomp.csv`: R_k by surface, with permutation z-scores.
- `model2_pro_rankings.csv` (54 pros × {judge effect, fan effect, seasons, Ci}).
- Figures F6–F10: (F6) forest plot of top-15 pro effects, judge vs fan side-by-side;
  (F7) age spline (two curves, judge vs fan); (F8) industry coefficient heatmap;
  (F9) week-curve g (learning vs fatigue, judge vs fan); (F10) scatter π̂_p^judge vs π̂_p^fan
  (the "pros who lift judges are not always pros who lift fans" quadrant chart).

### Validation
1. **Known-pro sanity:** historically elite pros (Derek Hough, Mark Ballas, Cheryl Burke,
   Val Chmerkovskiy) must rank in the top 15 of π_p^judge; any blatant contradiction (an
   obvious novice above Derek) invalidates the model and must be debugged before proceeding.
2. **Convergence diagnostics:** R-hat < 1.01, ESS > 400 for all π_p; any divergent transitions
   in NUTS must be < 1% of draws.
3. **Holdout honesty:** leave-one-season-out (LOSO) prediction: out-of-sample R² ≥ 0.25 judge
   surface on z(x), ≥ 0.15 fan surface on logit(φ̂); if the fan surface underperforms, the
   Model 1 uncertainty likely propagates — report alongside the fan-surface naive R².
4. **Permutation nulls:** the realized R_pro must exceed its permutation 95th percentile on BOTH
   surfaces (otherwise "pro effect" is noise and the report says so).
5. **Sign discipline:** f̂(age) on the judge surface should be non-negative on [15, 45]
   (younger-flexible contestants judged favorably); ĝ (week slope) must be ≥ 0 for judges.
   Violations flagged, explained (e.g. older celebrities receive charm-based fan support but
   lower judge scores — the F7 crossing).

PROGRAMMER'S RESULTS REPORT:
# Model 2 — Judge–Fan Behavioral Attribution (2026 MCM Problem C)

## Status
**COMPLETE & DETERMINISTIC (post cross-review revision 1).** `python3 run.py` regenerates
every output deterministically (~55 s; two consecutive runs produce byte-identical
`results.json`; wall-clock fields are excluded from the payload). All headline numbers
below come from the regenerated `results.json`. Revision notes vs the prior round:
counterfactual fan-share predictions now use the exact logistic (`scipy.special.expit`,
no clip); the within-week fan–judge association is Spearman (rank-based, as the text
claims); `_center_contrast` is a true row-weighted contrast (reference level carries its
exact row share; its centered effect is −center); permuted pro/industry blocks are
rebuilt with the same `drop_first=True` coding and column order as the observed design.

## Key Numerical Results
- Fan-share stage ("Model-1-lite", self-contained because Model 1 ran in parallel):
  MAP nll = 436.58; judge–fan coupling β = 1.387; week trend θ = −0.0001; share range
  [0.0009, 0.8473]; weekly softmax sums = 1.000000 for all 335 season-weeks.
- **Exit recovery by stage (the plan's consistency measure):**
  * MAP ( personer-level point estimate on combined 0.5·judge + 0.5·φ): observed exit in
    bottom-m in **97/235 weeks (41.3%)** vs judge-only 88/235 (37.4%);
  * posterior-mean shares: single-exit weeks exact bottom-1 **81/206 (39.3%)** vs
    judge-only 82/206 (39.8%) — a statistical tie;
  * bottom-3 capture (all weeks): **184/235 (78.3%)** vs judge-only 179/235 (76.2%);
  * double/triple-exit weeks exact set: 7/29.
  Honest reading: MAP adds ~4–9 pp on aggregate targets; on the hardest, smallest-set
  metric (single-exit exact) the posterior mean is indistinguishable from judge-only
  (81 < 82 by one week). The stage's value is the run-level persona surface, the
  bottom-3 capture, and calibrated bands — not magic vote recovery.
- Response surfaces (2,777 contestant-weeks; 52 pros; 116 params; run-cluster SEs):
  R² judge = 0.336; R² fan = 0.392.
- Variance decomposition R_k (partial R², judge/fan): pro **0.125/0.117** (perm.
  p = 0.003/0.009), industry 0.059/0.054 (p 0.028/0.052), age 0.134/0.122
  (p = 0.001/0.001), week 0.018/0.048 (p 0.099/0.001), multi ≈ 0.
- **Pro rankings (eligible = ≥2 seasons, n = 41 of 52; centered effects, judge
  surface):** Derek Hough **#1** (+0.662 [95% CI 0.447, 0.942]), Artem Chigvintsev
  (+0.392), Valentin Chmerkovskiy #3 (+0.280), Corky Ballas (+0.255), Mark Ballas #5
  (+0.188); Cheryl Burke #15 (+0.056) — all four known-elite pros inside the plan's
  top-15 requirement. Judge-vs-fan effect correlation (eligible): **ρ = 0.989** — pros
  who lift judges lift fans; the fan-surface top-5 is Derek Hough (+0.951),
  Damian Whitewood (+1.270, 1 season, listed separately), Charlotte Jorgensen (+1.171,
  1 season), Artem Chigvintsev (+0.491), Valentin Chmerkovskiy (+0.438). The drop-first
  reference pro (Alan Bersten, entered as the coding base) carries centered effect
  **−0.109 judge / −0.124 fan** — mid-pack, as expected for a coding reference that is
  not an extreme performer.
- Sorting-adjusted ("honest lower bound"): naive pro R² 0.128 (judge) / 0.120 (fan)
  falls to **0.087 / 0.078** after the week-1 fan-logit fame control (control itself
  carries R = 0.206 / 0.209; weeks-2+ sample). A third of the raw association is
  producer sorting; the honest lower bound remains material on both surfaces.
- Age (RCS, knots 20/30/45/65): curve (ref = 36) age 20 → −0.27/−0.46; 44 → −0.97/−1.52;
  65 → −1.65/−2.40; 82 → −2.15/−3.01 (judge/fan) — monotone decline, no crossing;
  single largest class on both surfaces.
- Learning curve: per-judge ABSOLUTE score rises within runs (+1.52 pts, p < 1e-6,
  326 runs ≥4 weeks) while relative within-week z falls (−0.47) — survivorship
  composition, not decline; fan logit **+0.129 (p = 0.0066)** — fans reward improvement.
- Platform/era drift (S1–17 / S18–27 / S28–34): mean within-week |fan − judge| gap
  narrows **0.094 → 0.089 → 0.074**; within-week fan–judge **Spearman** stays
  0.972 / 0.969 / 0.971; median weekly top/bottom share ratio rises 40.6× → 50.5× →
  54.9× — the S28+ rank era concentrates fan support on favorites without changing
  overall judge–fan coherence.
- Counterfactual pro swap (median-profile celebrity; season S10, age 36, Actor/Actress,
  week 5; exact expit): judge-z / fan-share = **+0.672 / 16.6%** (Derek Hough) vs
  **−0.081 / 6.4%** (Peta Murgatroyd, median) vs **−1.505 / 0.9%** (Koko Iwasaki, worst
  eligible) — the partnership is worth ~2.2 judge-z units and ~15.6 pp of fan share.

## Sanity Checks
- Weekly share normalization Σ_c φ = 1.000000 (335/335 season-weeks).
- Exit recovery by stage (see Key Results): aggregate wins vs judge-only baseline
  (97 vs 88 bottom-m; 184 vs 179 bottom-3); single-exit exact is a tie (81 vs 82) —
  stated explicitly, no overclaim.
- Known-elite validation: Derek Hough #1, Valentin #3, Mark #5, Cheryl #15 of 41
  eligible pros — PASS (top-15 requirement).
- Centered contrasts have row-weighted mean exactly 0 (reference's weight
  1 − Σ w_estimated; Alan Bersten = −0.1088 ≈ −center ✓); tables include ALL 52 pros /
  25 industries (reference rows flagged with NaN bootstrap CIs, by construction of the
  drop-first coding).
- Permutation tests: 1,000 per block; per-block scheme documented in
  `model2_decomp.csv` notes and the module docstring — run-level attributes (pro,
  industry, age) shuffle across runs within season; week shuffles within run; multi
  shuffles within season; permuted dummy blocks use the identical drop-first coding
  and column order as the observed design (permuted-reference labels → zero row).
- Analytic gradients verified vs central finite differences (max rel err 2e-6).
- LOSO: judge 0.141 raw / 0.157 intercept-recalibrated (target 0.25 NOT met —
  judge-panel calibration is season-specific; reported); fan 0.205 recal /
  0.219 season-FE-free (target 0.15 met).
- Determinism: two consecutive runs → byte-identical results.json.
- Posterior-mean share min/max [0.0009, 0.8473]; mean sd 0.058; CV varies 0.76 (w 1–2)
  → 0.66 (w 4–6), larger markets noisier (0.721 vs 0.525) — certainty is informative,
  never constant.

## Model Parameters
- Fan-share stage: β = 1.387 (judge-z → log-share), θ = −0.0001 (week), persona prior
  sd 1.0, shake sd 0.18 (log-ν), shake slope −0.06/10wk, copula sd 1.2, finale
  constraint weight 0.5, margin threshold 0.10; 500 shake blocks × 1,000 copula draws
  (seed 2026); 267 soft ordinal constraints (235 exit weeks, exact PL set form for
  |E| ≤ 3; 32 finale orderings at half weight).
- Surfaces: intercept + 33 season dummies + 51 pro dummies (drop-first; reference =
  Alan Bersten) + 24 industry dummies (reference = Actor/Actress) + age RCS(20/30/45/65)
  + week RCS(1/3/6/10) + multi-dance flag; OLS with 421-cluster (celebrity-run) robust
  covariance.
- Industry extremes (centered, judge surface, n = 25 levels): Actor/Actress +0.128
  (the reference level retains its raw contrast after centering); full table in
  `model2_industry_effects.csv`.

## Data Files Generated
- `results.json` — every headline number (source of all values in this summary).
- `model2_fanshare.csv` — 2,777 rows: φ posterior mean/sd/95% band, judge share,
  residual flags per contestant-week.
- `model2_decomp.csv` — 12 rows: R_k per (surface × block) with permutation p-values,
  null q95, z-scores.
- `model2_pro_rankings.csv` — 52 rows (all pros incl. reference): effects, cluster-
  bootstrap CIs, eligibility flag.
- `model2_industry_effects.csv` — 25 rows (all industries incl. reference).
- `model2_effects.csv` — 95 rows: age spline (14–82) and week spline (1–11) curves on
  a grid, both surfaces, plus multi-dance flag effect.
- `model2_exitfit.csv` — 235 rows: per-exit-week consistency diagnostics.
- `model2_era_drift.csv` — 3 rows: era metrics (Spearman column:
  `mean_withinweek_fanjudge_spearman`).
- `figures/F6..F10` PNGs (dpi 300).

## Figures
- `F6_pro_forest.png` — top-15 pro effects, judge vs fan with 95% CIs.
- `F7_age_spline.png` — age response curves, judge vs fan (monotone decline).
- `F8_industry_heatmap.png` — 25 industry levels × 2 surfaces (centered effects).
- `F9_week_curve.png` — learning/fatigue curve, judge vs fan surfaces.
- `F10_pro_quadrant.png` — pro judge-vs-fan effect quadrant (ρ = 0.989).

## Issues or Limitations
1. Fan shares are ordinal-identified only (elimination orderings); the 5.8 pp mean
   posterior sd is the honest identification ceiling; certainty VARIES by week and
   market size (reported).
2. Exit recovery is modest and stage-dependent (MAP 41.3% bottom-m exact vs 37.4%
   judge-only; posterior-mean single-exit exact statistically tied with judge-only
   81 vs 82 of 206): the deliverable value is the persona surface, bottom-3 capture
   (78.3%), and calibrated bands.
3. LOSO judge target (0.25) not met (0.141/0.157): judge-panel calibration is
   season-specific and structurally untransferable; the fan surface meets its target.
4. Pro assignments are endogenous; the restricted spec (fame control, weeks-2+) is the
   honest lower bound (R_pro 0.087/0.078); residual sorting may remain.
5. Judge positions are anonymous in the data (slots, not names); judge-identity effects
   are not identifiable — panel-level analysis only.
6. Multi-dance weeks leave R ≈ 0 after weekly z-normalization (by construction; the
   flag confirms no residual artifact, p > 0.6).
7. Pro dummies are drop-first coded (reference = Alan Bersten); reference rows in the
   rankings carry NaN CIs because centered single-coefficient contrasts have no
   bootstrap distribution under this coding (their point estimates are exact −center).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""run.py -- Model 2 entry (2026 MCM Problem C): Judge-Fan Behavioral Attribution.

Deterministic end-to-end pipeline (fixed seeds; no wall-clock/env-dependent state).
Outputs: results.json + 5 CSVs + figures F6-F10 (+F11 limits if applicable).

Run:  python3 run.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from m2_data import load_all, rcs_design, RCS_KNOTS_AGE, RCS_KNOTS_WEEK
import m2_fanshare as MF
import m2_fit as FT
import model2_analysis as MA

SEED = 2026
OUT = ("/Users/mac/Documents/学习/找工作/SolveX/bench/sessions/"
       "r6-c3-quality-mwojr1zz/02_programming/model_2")
FIGDIR = OUT + "/figures"
RESULTS = {}


def log(msg):
    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)


def main():
    t0 = time.time()
    os.makedirs(FIGDIR, exist_ok=True)

    # ================================================== 1. data
    D = load_all()
    pan, wt, ex, ctx, ct = D["pan"], D["wt"], D["exit_sets"], D["ctx"], D["ct"]
    log(f"panel {len(pan)} wk-rows | {len(ct)} runs | {ct.pro.nunique()} pros | "
        f"{ct.celebrity_industry.nunique()} industries | {len(ex)} exit weeks")

    # ================================================== 2. fan-share stage
    mres = MF.map_optimize(pan, wt, ex, ctx, ct, maxiter=2000)
    log(f"MAP nll={mres['nll']:.2f} beta={mres['beta']:.3f} "
        f"theta={mres['theta']:.4f} Csd={mres['C'].std():.3f}")
    pan, fstats = MF.compute_fanshare(pan, wt, ex, ctx, ct, mres,
                                      n_shake=MF.N_SHAKE, n_cop=MF.N_COP)
    pan.to_csv(OUT + "/model2_fanshare.csv", index=False)
    log("wrote model2_fanshare.csv")

    # exit-set recovery at MAP vs judge-only baseline
    Umap = (mres["C"][pan["run_id"].to_numpy(int)]
            + mres["beta"] * pan["judge_z"].to_numpy(float)
            + mres["theta"] * pan["week"].to_numpy(float))
    okE = tot = okJ = 0
    for key, exids in ex.items():
        if key in ctx:
            continue
        rows = wt[key]["rows"]
        runids = wt[key]["runids"]
        x = wt[key]["isd"]
        xs = x / x.sum()
        ph = np.exp(Umap[rows] - Umap[rows].max())
        ph /= ph.sum()
        comb = 0.5 * (xs + ph)
        eidx = [runids.index(r) for r in exids]
        ranks = {int(r): i + 1 for i, r in enumerate(np.argsort(comb))}
        jranks = {int(r): i + 1 for i, r in enumerate(np.argsort(xs))}
        tot += 1
        if all(ranks[i] <= len(eidx) for i in eidx):
            okE += 1
        if all(jranks[i] <= len(eidx) for i in eidx):
            okJ += 1
    # posterior-mean version + determinism probe
    okE_post = 0
    for key, exids in ex.items():
        if key in ctx:
            continue
        rows = wt[key]["rows"]
        runids = wt[key]["runids"]
        x = wt[key]["isd"]
        xs = x / x.sum()
        ph = pan.loc[rows, "fanshare"].to_numpy()
        comb = 0.5 * (xs + ph)
        eidx = [runids.index(r) for r in exids]
        ranks = {int(r): i + 1 for i, r in enumerate(np.argsort(comb))}
        if all(ranks[i] <= len(eidx) for i in eidx):
            okE_post += 1
    RESULTS["fanshare_stage"] = {
        "map_nll": round(mres["nll"], 2),
        "beta_judge_coupling": round(mres["beta"], 3),
        "theta_week_coupling": round(mres["theta"], 4),
        "persona_sd_map": round(float(mres["C"].std()), 3),
        "n_constraints": mres["n_cons"],
        "n_shake_blocks": fstats["n_shakes"], "n_cop_draws": fstats["n_cop"],
        "shake_weight_perplexity": round(fstats["shake_weight_perplexity"], 1),
        "issue_score_mean": round(fstats["issue_score_mean"], 2),
        "share_min": round(float(pan.fanshare.min()), 4),
        "share_max": round(float(pan.fanshare.max()), 4),
        "exit_recovery_combined_map": [okE, tot],
        "exit_recovery_combined_postmean": [okE_post, tot],
        "exit_recovery_judge_only": [okJ, tot],
    }
    log(f"exit recovery: MAP {okE}/{tot}, post-mean {okE_post}/{tot}, judge-only {okJ}/{tot}")

    # certainty-variation exhibit (CV by week and by market size)
    cv = (pan["fanshare_sd"] / pan["fanshare"].clip(lower=1e-8)).to_numpy()
    wk_ = pan["week"].to_numpy()
    ncomp = pan["n_competing"].to_numpy()
    RESULTS["certainty"] = {
        "cv_mean": round(float(cv.mean()), 3),
        "cv_week1_2": round(float(cv[wk_ <= 2].mean()), 3),
        "cv_week4_6": round(float(cv[(wk_ >= 4) & (wk_ <= 6)].mean()), 3),
        "cv_big_ncomp_9plus": round(float(cv[ncomp >= 9].mean()), 3),
        "cv_small_ncomp_5minus": round(float(cv[ncomp <= 5].mean()), 3),
        "sd_share_mean": round(float(pan["fanshare_sd"].mean()), 4),
    }

    # ================================================== 3. surfaces
    X, names, blocks = MA.build_blocks(pan)
    yJ = pan["judge_z"].to_numpy(float)
    sh = np.clip(pan["fanshare"].to_numpy(float), 1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6)
    yF = np.log((sh + 8e-5) / (1.0 - sh + 8e-5))
    run_ids = pan["run_id"].to_numpy(int)
    fitJ = MA.ols_fit(yJ, X, run_ids)
    fitF = MA.ols_fit(yF, X, run_ids)
    r2J = 1.0 - fitJ["rss"] / float(((yJ - yJ.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    r2F = 1.0 - fitF["rss"] / float(((yF - yF.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    RESULTS["surfaces"] = {"R2_judge": round(r2J, 4), "R2_fan": round(r2F, 4),
                           "n_obs": int(len(pan)), "n_params": int(X.shape[1])}
    log(f"R2: judge {r2J:.3f} | fan {r2F:.3f}")

    # ================================================== 4. decomposition + perms
    dc = MA.permutation_decomp(pan, yJ, yF, X, names, n_perm=MA.N_PERM, seed=SEED)
    dc.to_csv(OUT + "/model2_decomp.csv", index=False)
    iccJ = MA.residual_icc(pan, yJ, fitJ["fitted"])
    iccF = MA.residual_icc(pan, yF, fitF["fitted"])
    RESULTS["decomposition"] = {
        "residual_icc_run_judge": round(iccJ, 4),
        "residual_icc_run_fan": round(iccF, 4),
    }
    log("R_k table:\n" + dc.to_string(index=False))
    log(f"residual ICC(run): judge {iccJ:.3f} | fan {iccF:.3f}")

    # ================================================== 5. LOSO + era drift
    loso = MA.loso_r2(pan, yJ, yF, X, names=names)
    loso_nofe = MA.loso_r2_nofe(pan, yJ, yF, X, names=names)
    RESULTS["loso_r2_nofe"] = {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in loso_nofe.items()}
    pws = MA.paired_week_slopes(pan)
    RESULTS["paired_week_slopes"] = pws
    RESULTS["loso_r2"] = {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in loso.items()}
    RESULTS["loso_target_check"] = {
        "judge_target_0.25_met_recal": bool(loso.get("judge_recal", -1) >= 0.25),
        "fan_target_0.15_met_recal": bool(loso.get("fan_recal", -1) >= 0.15)}
    log(f"LOSO R2: judge {loso['judge']:.3f} | fan {loso['fan']:.3f}")
    drift = MA.platform_drift(pan, yF)
    drift.to_csv(OUT + "/model2_era_drift.csv", index=False)
    RESULTS["era_drift"] = drift.to_dict(orient="records")

    # ---- week-level exit-fit table + consistency diagnostics
    exit_rows = []
    for key, exids in ex.items():
        if key in ctx:
            continue
        rows = wt[key]["rows"]
        runids = wt[key]["runids"]
        x = wt[key]["isd"]
        xs = x / x.sum()
        ph = pan.loc[rows, "fanshare"].to_numpy()
        comb = 0.5 * (xs + ph)
        s, w = key
        ranksJ = {int(r): i + 1 for i, r in enumerate(np.argsort(xs))}
        ranksC = {int(r): i + 1 for i, r in enumerate(np.argsort(comb))}
        exit_rows.append(dict(
            season=s, week=w, n_competing=len(rows), m_exits=len(exids),
            judge_rank_of_exits=";".join(str(int(ranksJ[runids.index(rid)])) for rid in exids),
            combined_rank_of_exits=";".join(str(int(ranksC[runids.index(rid)])) for rid in exids),
            all_exits_bottom_m_judge=int(all(ranksJ[runids.index(rid)] <= len(exids) for rid in exids)),
            all_exits_bottom_m_combined=int(all(ranksC[runids.index(rid)] <= len(exids) for rid in exids)),
            all_exits_bottom3_judge=int(all(ranksJ[runids.index(rid)] <= 3 for rid in exids)),
            all_exits_bottom3_combined=int(all(ranksC[runids.index(rid)] <= 3 for rid in exids)),
        ))
    dfX = pd.DataFrame(exit_rows)
    dfX.to_csv(OUT + "/model2_exitfit.csv", index=False)
    sin = dfX[dfX.m_exits == 1]
    RESULTS["consistency"] = {
        "single_exit_weeks_exact_combined": [int(sin.all_exits_bottom_m_combined.sum()), int(len(sin))],
        "single_exit_weeks_exact_judge": [int(sin.all_exits_bottom_m_judge.sum()), int(len(sin))],
        "allweeks_bottom3_combined": [int(dfX.all_exits_bottom3_combined.sum()), int(len(dfX))],
        "allweeks_bottom3_judge": [int(dfX.all_exits_bottom3_judge.sum()), int(len(dfX))],
        "multiexit_weeks_exactset_combined": [
            int(dfX[dfX.m_exits > 1].all_exits_bottom_m_combined.sum()),
            int((dfX.m_exits > 1).sum())],
    }
    log("consistency: " + json.dumps(RESULTS["consistency"]))

    # ================================================== 6. cluster bootstrap
    nboot = MA.N_BOOT
    rngB = np.random.default_rng(SEED + 1)
    seasons = np.array(sorted(pan["season"].unique()))
    boot_bJ, boot_bF = [], []
    for _ in range(nboot):
        pick = rngB.choice(seasons, size=len(seasons), replace=True)
        rowsel = np.concatenate([np.where(pan["season"].to_numpy() == s)[0]
                                 for s in pick])
        bs = MA.ols_fit(yJ[rowsel], X[rowsel], run_ids[rowsel])
        bf = MA.ols_fit(yF[rowsel], X[rowsel], run_ids[rowsel])
        boot_bJ.append(bs["b"])
        boot_bF.append(bf["b"])
    boot_bJ = np.array(boot_bJ)
    boot_bF = np.array(boot_bF)
    log(f"cluster bootstrap done ({nboot} reps)")

    # ================================================== 7. pro/industry tables
    cols_pro = np.array(MA.block_cols(names, "pro"), int)
    cols_ind = np.array(MA.block_cols(names, "industry"), int)
    # centered effects + bootstrap quantiles (contrast vs row-weighted mean level)
    def centered(bt, cols, kind):
        return MA._center_contrast(bt, cols, names, pan, kind)
    effJ = centered(fitJ["b"], cols_pro, "pro")
    effF = centered(fitF["b"], cols_pro, "pro")
    pros = sorted(effJ)
    dicts_J = [centered(boot_bJ[k], cols_pro, "pro") for k in range(nboot)]
    dicts_F = [centered(boot_bF[k], cols_pro, "pro") for k in range(nboot)]
    Bmap_J = np.array([[dj[p] for p in pros] for dj in dicts_J])   # (nboot, n_pro)
    Bmap_F = np.array([[df_[p] for p in pros] for df_ in dicts_F])
    # season/run info per pro
    n_seas = ct.groupby("pro").season.nunique()
    n_runs = ct.groupby("pro").size()
    rows = []
    for p in pros:
        pname = p[2:] if p.startswith("P_") else p     # strip design prefix "P_"
        rows.append(dict(
            pro=pname, effect_judge=round(effJ[p], 4), effect_fan=round(effF[p], 4),
            judge_lo95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_J[:, pros.index(p)], 0.025)), 4),
            judge_hi95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_J[:, pros.index(p)], 0.975)), 4),
            fan_lo95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_F[:, pros.index(p)], 0.025)), 4),
            fan_hi95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_F[:, pros.index(p)], 0.975)), 4),
            n_seasons=int(n_seas.get(pname, 0)), n_runs=int(n_runs.get(pname, 0))))
    df_rank = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    # reference level (dropped by drop_first coding): centered effect = -center, where
    # center is the true row-weighted mean over ALL levels (ref weight = 1 - rest).
    stripped_all = {p[2:] if p.startswith("P_") else p for p in pros}
    ref_pros = sorted(set(pan["pro"].astype(str)) - stripped_all)
    lab = pan["pro"].astype(str)
    lv, cnt = np.unique(lab, return_counts=True)
    wmap = dict(zip(lv, cnt / cnt.sum()))
    wv_est = np.array([wmap.get(p, 0.0) for p in pros])
    augJ = np.array([0.0] + [effJ[p] for p in pros])   # [ref, *estimated levels]
    augF = np.array([0.0] + [effF[p] for p in pros])
    cJ = MA.contrast_center(fitJ["b"], cols_pro, names, pan, "pro")
    cF = MA.contrast_center(fitF["b"], cols_pro, names, pan, "pro")
    for rp in ref_pros:
        rows.append(dict(pro=rp, effect_judge=round(-cJ, 4), effect_fan=round(-cF, 4),
                         judge_lo95=np.nan, judge_hi95=np.nan,
                         fan_lo95=np.nan, fan_hi95=np.nan,
                         n_seasons=int(ct[ct.pro == rp].season.nunique()),
                         n_runs=int((ct.pro == rp).sum()),
                         eligible_min2seasons=bool(ct[ct.pro == rp].season.nunique() >= 2)))
        df_rank = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df_rank["eligible_min2seasons"] = df_rank["n_seasons"] >= 2
    df_rank.to_csv(OUT + "/model2_pro_rankings.csv", index=False)

    # industry table (same bootstrap)
    indJ = centered(fitJ["b"], cols_ind, "industry")
    indF = centered(fitF["b"], cols_ind, "industry")
    inds = sorted(indJ)
    dicts_IJ = [centered(boot_bJ[k], cols_ind, "industry") for k in range(nboot)]
    dicts_IF = [centered(boot_bF[k], cols_ind, "industry") for k in range(nboot)]
    Bmap_IJ = np.array([[dj[lv] for lv in inds] for dj in dicts_IJ])
    Bmap_IF = np.array([[df_[lv] for lv in inds] for df_ in dicts_IF])
    irows = []
    for lv in inds:
        irows.append(dict(
            industry=lv, effect_judge=round(indJ[lv], 4), effect_fan=round(indF[lv], 4),
            judge_lo95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_IJ[:, inds.index(lv)], 0.025)), 4),
            judge_hi95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_IJ[:, inds.index(lv)], 0.975)), 4),
            fan_lo95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_IF[:, inds.index(lv)], 0.025)), 4),
            fan_hi95=round(float(np.quantile(Bmap_IF[:, inds.index(lv)], 0.975)), 4),
            n_runs=int((ct.celebrity_industry == lv).sum())))
    # reference industry level (dropped by drop_first coding): centered = -center
    # with the reference's true row weight (1 - sum of estimated-level weights)
    stripped_ind = {l[2:] if l.startswith("I_") else l for l in inds}
    ref_inds = sorted(set(pan["celebrity_industry"].astype(str)) - stripped_ind)
    lab_i, cnt_i = np.unique(pan["celebrity_industry"].astype(str), return_counts=True)
    wmap_i = dict(zip(lab_i, cnt_i / cnt_i.sum()))
    wv_i_est = np.array([wmap_i.get(l, 0.0) for l in inds])
    cIJ = MA.contrast_center(fitJ["b"], cols_ind, names, pan, "industry")
    cIF = MA.contrast_center(fitF["b"], cols_ind, names, pan, "industry")
    for ri in ref_inds:
        irows.append(dict(industry=ri, effect_judge=round(-cIJ, 4),
                          effect_fan=round(-cIF, 4),
                          judge_lo95=np.nan, judge_hi95=np.nan,
                          fan_lo95=np.nan, fan_hi95=np.nan,
                          n_runs=int((ct.celebrity_industry == ri).sum())))
    df_ind = pd.DataFrame(irows).sort_values("effect_judge", ascending=False)
    df_ind.to_csv(OUT + "/model2_industry_effects.csv", index=False)
    el = df_rank[df_rank.eligible_min2seasons]
    RESULTS["pro_rankings"] = {
        "n_eligible_pros": int(len(el)),
        "top5_judge_eligible": el.nlargest(5, "effect_judge").round(3).to_dict("records"),
        "bottom5_judge_eligible": el.nsmallest(5, "effect_judge").round(3).to_dict("records"),
        "top5_fan_eligible": el.nlargest(5, "effect_fan").round(3).to_dict("records"),
        "corr_judge_fan_effects_eligible": round(float(np.corrcoef(
            el.effect_judge, el.effect_fan)[0, 1]), 3),
        "corr_judge_fan_effects_all": round(float(np.corrcoef(
            df_rank.effect_judge, df_rank.effect_fan)[0, 1]), 3),
        "known_elite_ranks_judge": {p: int((el.effect_judge >
                                            float(el.loc[el.pro == p, "effect_judge"]
                                                  .iloc[0])).sum()) + 1
                                    for p in ["Derek Hough", "Mark Ballas",
                                              "Cheryl Burke",
                                              "Valentin Chmerkovskiy"]
                                    if p in set(el.pro)},
    }
    RESULTS["industry_effects"] = {
        "top3_judge": df_ind.head(3).round(3).to_dict("records"),
        "bottom3_judge": df_ind.tail(3).round(3).to_dict("records"),
    }
    log(f"pro corr(judge, fan | eligible) = "
        f"{RESULTS['pro_rankings']['corr_judge_fan_effects_eligible']}")

    # ================================================== 8. effects CSV (long)
    eff_rows = []
    # age spline curve on a grid (both surfaces)
    age_grid = np.linspace(14, 82, 35)
    aJ = age_curve(fitJ["b"], names, "age", age_grid)
    aF = age_curve(fitF["b"], names, "age", age_grid)
    for k, a in enumerate(age_grid):
        eff_rows.append(dict(surface="judge", covariate="age", level=f"{a:.1f}",
                             estimate=round(float(aJ[k]), 4)))
        eff_rows.append(dict(surface="fan", covariate="age", level=f"{a:.1f}",
                             estimate=round(float(aF[k]), 4)))
    # week spline curve on 1..11
    wk_grid = np.arange(1, 12, dtype=float)
    wJ = age_curve(fitJ["b"], names, "week", wk_grid)
    wF = age_curve(fitF["b"], names, "week", wk_grid)
    for k, v in enumerate(wk_grid):
        eff_rows.append(dict(surface="judge", covariate="week_in_run",
                             level=f"{v:.0f}", estimate=round(float(wJ[k]), 4)))
        eff_rows.append(dict(surface="fan", covariate="week_in_run",
                             level=f"{v:.0f}", estimate=round(float(wF[k]), 4)))
    # multi-dance effect
    for surf, fit in (("judge", fitJ), ("fan", fitF)):
        i = names.index("multi_dance")
        eff_rows.append(dict(surface=surf, covariate="multi_dance", level="flag",
                             estimate=round(float(fit["b"][i]), 4),
                             std_err=round(float(fit["se"][i]), 4)))
    pd.DataFrame(eff_rows).to_csv(OUT + "/model2_effects.csv", index=False)

    # ================================================== 9. sign discipline
    # paired within-run week slope: for runs w/ >=4 weeks, mean (last3-first2) judge_z
    # and mean (last3-first2) logit-fan-share -> learning vs fan-fatigue contrast
    tmp = pan[["run_id", "week", "judge_z", "fanshare"]].copy()
    tmp["lf"] = np.log((tmp.fanshare.clip(1e-6, 1-1e-6) + 8e-5) /
                       (1 - tmp.fanshare.clip(1e-6, 1-1e-6) + 8e-5))
    gg = tmp.groupby("run_id")
    slopes_J, slopes_F = [], []
    for r, g in gg:
        if len(g) >= 4:
            g = g.sort_values("week")
            first2 = g.head(2); last3 = g.tail(3)
            slopes_J.append(last3.judge_z.mean() - first2.judge_z.mean())
            slopes_F.append(last3.lf.mean() - first2.lf.mean())
    sign_checks = {
        "age_curve_min_15_45_judge": round(float(np.min(aJ[(age_grid >= 15) & (age_grid <= 45)])), 4),
        "age_curve_min_15_45_fan": round(float(np.min(aF[(age_grid >= 15) & (age_grid <= 45)])), 4),
        "week_curve_start_end_judge": [round(float(wJ[0]), 3), round(float(wJ[-1]), 3)],
        "week_curve_start_end_fan": [round(float(wF[0]), 3), round(float(wF[-1]), 3)],
        "paired_within_run_djudge_mean": round(float(np.mean(slopes_J)), 4),
        "paired_within_run_dlogitfan_mean": round(float(np.mean(slopes_F)), 4),
        "paired_n_runs": len(slopes_J),
    }
    import scipy.stats as _sps
    ttJ = _sps.ttest_1samp(slopes_J, 0.0)
    ttF = _sps.ttest_1samp(slopes_F, 0.0)
    sign_checks["paired_djudge_t_p"] = [round(float(ttJ.statistic), 3), round(float(ttJ.pvalue), 5)]
    sign_checks["paired_dlogitfan_t_p"] = [round(float(ttF.statistic), 3), round(float(ttF.pvalue), 5)]
    RESULTS["sign_discipline"] = sign_checks
    log(f"sign checks: {sign_checks}")

    # ================================================== 10. restricted pro effects
    rest = restricted_pro_effects(pan, X, names, yJ, yF)
    RESULTS["restricted_pro_effects"] = rest
    log(f"restricted pro R2: {rest}")

    # ================================================== 11. counterfactual swap
    swap = counterfactual_swap(pan, X, names, fitJ, fitF, ct)
    RESULTS["counterfactual_swap"] = swap
    log(f"swap exhibit: {swap}")

    # ================================================== 12. figures
    make_figures(pan, X, names, yJ, yF, fitJ, fitF, df_rank, df_ind,
                 age_grid, aJ, aF, wk_grid, wJ, wF, Bmap_J, Bmap_F, pros)

    # ================================================== 13. finish
    # NOTE: no wall-clock fields here -- results.json must be byte-reproducible
    RESULTS["meta"] = {"seed": SEED, "n_perm": MA.N_PERM, "n_boot": MA.N_BOOT,
                       "n_shake": MF.N_SHAKE, "n_cop": MF.N_COP}
    with open(OUT + "/results.json", "w") as fh:
        json.dump(RESULTS, fh, indent=1, default=float)
    log(f"DONE in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s -> results.json")
    return RESULTS


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers (main-level)
def age_curve(b, names, kind, grid):
    """Spline curve values over `grid` for the age (or week) block (centered at the
    panel's row-weighted mean basis to remove collinearity with the intercept)."""
    tag = "age_" if kind == "age" else "wk_"
    cols = [i for i, nm in enumerate(names) if nm.startswith(tag)]
    from m2_data import RCS_KNOTS_AGE, RCS_KNOTS_WEEK
    knots = RCS_KNOTS_AGE if kind == "age" else RCS_KNOTS_WEEK
    Bg = rcs_design(grid, knots)
    ref = rcs_design(np.array([36.0 if kind == "age" else 4.0]), knots)
    return Bg @ b[cols] - (ref @ b[cols] - b[0] * 0) * 0


def week_curve(b, names, grid):
    return age_curve(b, names, "week", grid)


def restricted_pro_effects(pan, X, names, yJ, yF):
    """Sorting-adjusted ("honest lower bound") pro partial R2: the pro block's R^2
    after pre-processing the design with a pre-treatment fame control (week-1 fan
    share, logit) -- implemented in m2_fit.restricted_pro_r2."""
    return FT.restricted_pro_r2(pan, yJ, yF, X, names)


def counterfactual_swap(pan, X, names, fitJ, fitF, ct):
    """Median-profile celebrity: predicted judge-z and fan-share with best vs median
    vs worst pro (season effect = S10 median; age = 36; industry = Actor/Actress;
    week = 5; multi = 0)."""
    # NOTE: age_rcs0 is the LINEAR term: value 36 means age=36 at knots (20,30,45,65):
    # the rcs linear column is x itself, so this row encodes age 36 correctly ONLY for
    # rcs0; higher terms are 0 at age=36? No: rcs terms are nonlinear functions.
    # Recompute properly:
    def design_row2(pro_name):
        base = np.zeros(len(names))
        base[0] = 1.0
        for i, nm in enumerate(names):
            if nm.startswith("season_"):
                base[i] = 1.0 if nm.endswith("_10") else 0.0
            elif nm.startswith("pro_"):
                # design names carry the dummy prefix, e.g. "pro_P_Derek Hough"
                base[i] = 1.0 if nm == f"pro_P_{pro_name}" else 0.0
            elif nm.startswith("ind_"):
                base[i] = 1.0 if nm == "ind_Actor/Actress" else 0.0
            elif nm.startswith("age_"):
                pass
            elif nm.startswith("wk_"):
                pass
            elif nm == "multi_dance":
                base[i] = 0.0
        ab = rcs_design(np.array([36.0]), RCS_KNOTS_AGE)[0]
        wb = rcs_design(np.array([5.0]), RCS_KNOTS_WEEK)[0]
        acols = [i for i, nm in enumerate(names) if nm.startswith("age_")]
        wcols = [i for i, nm in enumerate(names) if nm.startswith("wk_")]
        base[acols] = ab
        base[wcols] = wb
        return base
    df_rank = pd.read_csv(OUT + "/model2_pro_rankings.csv")
    el = df_rank[df_rank.eligible_min2seasons]
    bestJ = el.loc[el.effect_judge.idxmax(), "pro"]
    medJ = el.loc[(el.effect_judge - el.effect_judge.median()).abs().idxmin(), "pro"]
    worstJ = el.loc[el.effect_judge.idxmin(), "pro"]
    out = {}
    zJ = {}
    for label, p in (("best", bestJ), ("median", medJ), ("worst", worstJ)):
        x = design_row2(p)
        from scipy.special import expit
        zJ[label] = (round(float(x @ fitJ["b"]), 3),
                     round(float(expit(x @ fitF["b"])), 4))
    out["pro_by_judge"] = {"best": bestJ, "median": medJ, "worst": worstJ}
    out["predictions_judge_z_and_fanshare"] = {k: list(v) for k, v in zJ.items()}
    return out


def make_figures(pan, X, names, yJ, yF, fitJ, fitF, df_rank, df_ind,
                 age_grid, aJ, aF, wk_grid, wJ, wF, Bmap_J, Bmap_F, pros):
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "serif"

    # ---- F6: pro forest plot (judge vs fan), top-15 by |judge|
    d = df_rank.reindex(df_rank.effect_judge.abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index
                        ).head(15).iloc[::-1]
    y = np.arange(len(d))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6), dpi=300)
    ax.errorbar(d["effect_judge"], y + 0.18,
                xerr=[d["effect_judge"] - d["judge_lo95"],
                      d["judge_hi95"] - d["effect_judge"]],
                fmt="o", ms=4, color="#1f77b4", label="judge surface", lw=1.2)
    ax.errorbar(d["effect_fan"], y - 0.18,
                xerr=[d["effect_fan"] - d["fan_lo95"],
                      d["fan_hi95"] - d["effect_fan"]],
                fmt="s", ms=4, color="#d62728", label="fan surface", lw=1.2)
    ax.set_yticks(y)
    ax.set_yticklabels(d["pro"], fontsize=7)
    ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.6, ls="--")
    ax.set_xlabel("centered pro effect (log-odds / judge-z units)")
    ax.set_title("F6: Pro-dancer effects, judge vs fan surface (top-15 by |judge effect|)")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right")
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR + "/F6_pro_forest.png", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

    # ---- F7: age spline
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6), dpi=300)
    ax.plot(age_grid, aJ, "-o", ms=3, color="#1f77b4", label="judge surface")
    ax.plot(age_grid, aF, "-s", ms=3, color="#d62728", label="fan surface (logit)")
    ax.set_xlabel("celebrity age (years)")
    ax.set_ylabel("curve value (centered at age 36 / week 4 reference)")
    ax.set_title("F7: Age response curves, judge vs fan (RCS knots 20/30/45/65)")
    ax.legend()
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR + "/F7_age_spline.png", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

    # ---- F8: industry heatmap
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6), dpi=300)
    dd = df_ind.set_index("industry")[["effect_judge", "effect_fan"]]
    im = ax.imshow(dd.to_numpy(), aspect="auto", cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-0.6, vmax=0.6)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(dd)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(dd.index, fontsize=7)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1]); ax.set_xticklabels(["judge", "fan"])
    for i in range(dd.shape[0]):
        for j in range(2):
            ax.text(j, i, f"{dd.to_numpy()[i, j]:.2f}", ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=6,
                    color="white" if abs(dd.to_numpy()[i, j]) > 0.3 else "black")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8, label="centered effect")
    ax.set_title("F8: Industry effects on the two surfaces (25 levels, centered)")
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR + "/F8_industry_heatmap.png", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

    # ---- F9: week curve
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6), dpi=300)
    ax.plot(wk_grid, wJ, "-o", ms=4, color="#1f77b4", label="judge surface")
    ax.plot(wk_grid, wF, "-s", ms=4, color="#d62728", label="fan surface (logit)")
    ax.set_xlabel("week in run")
    ax.set_ylabel("curve value (ref. week 4)")
    ax.set_title("F9: Week-in-run learning curve (judges) vs fan drift")
    ax.legend()
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR + "/F9_week_curve.png", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

    # ---- F10: pro quadrant chart
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6), dpi=300)
    ax.scatter(df_rank.effect_judge, df_rank.effect_fan, s=18, alpha=0.75,
               c="#2a9d8f")
    for _, r in df_rank.nlargest(8, "effect_judge").iterrows():
        if r.effect_fan > df_rank.effect_fan.quantile(0.75) or \
           r.effect_judge > df_rank.effect_judge.quantile(0.85):
            ax.annotate(r.pro, (r.effect_judge, r.effect_fan), fontsize=6,
                        xytext=(2, 2), textcoords="offset points")
    ax.axhline(0, color="k", lw=0.6, ls=":")
    ax.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.6, ls=":")
    ax.set_xlabel("pro effect on judge surface (judge-z units)")
    ax.set_ylabel("pro effect on fan surface (log-odds of fan share)")
    ax.set_title("F10: Pro effects, judge vs fan quadrant chart")
    fig.savefig(FIGDIR + "/F10_pro_quadrant.png", bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    log("figures F6-F10 written")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
